citations.quote:
2.1 Electrolyte and pouch cell preparation
Battery grade solvents of propylene carbonate (PC), ethylene carbonate (EC), ethyl methyl carbonate (EMC), dimethyl carbonate (DMC), diethyl carbonate (DEC) and fluoroethylene carbonate (FEC) were obtained from Shenzhen CAPCHEM Technology Co., Ltd, China, and used as received. Sodium hexafluorophosphate $(\mathrm{NaPF}_6$ , KISHIDA Chemical Co., Ltd, Japan) was dissolved into cold solvent mixtures with different volume ratios. Water contents of all resultant electrolytes were determined by the Karl Fischer titration to be lower than $15~\mathrm{ppm}$ .

The $NaNi_{1/3}Fe_{1/3}Mn_{1/3}O_{2}$ (NFM) cathode material was scale-up synthesized as described previously [17]. The NFM cathode and hard carbon (HC) anode were prepared by coating slurries consisting of 92 wt.% active material, 4 wt.% super P, and 4 wt.% polyvinylidene fluoride (PVDF) in N-Methyl-2-pyrrolidone (NMP) onto an aluminum foil, respectively. The cathode-separator-anode assembles were stacked and packaged into a plastic-laminated aluminum pouch. After heating at 80 °C for 48 h under vacuum, the dried pouch cells were moved into a glove box for injecting electrolyte.

citations.quote: Electrolyte design strategies are closely related to the capacities, cycle life and safety of sodium-ion batteries. In this study, we are aimed to optimize electrolyte with the focus on engineering aspects. The basic physicochemical properties including ionic conductivity, viscosity, wettability and thermochemical stability of the electrolytes using $\mathrm{NaPF}_6$ as the solute and the mixed solvent with different components of EMC, DMC or DEC in PC or EC were systematically measured. Ah pouch cell with $\mathrm{NaNi}_{1/3}\mathrm{Fe}_{1/3}\mathrm{Mn}_{1/3}\mathrm{O}_2/$ hard carbon electrodes was used to evaluate the performance of the prepared electrolytes. By using the Inductive Coupled Plasma Emission Spectrometer (ICP), X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS), Thermogravimetric-differential scanning calorimetry (TG-DSC) and Accelerating Rate Calorimeter (ARC), we show that an optimized electrolyte can effectively promote the formation of a protective interfacial layer on two electrodes, which not only retards parasitic reactions between the electrodes and electrolyte but also suppresses dissolution of metal ions from the cathode. association_citations.quote: Therefore, in the present work, the PC/EMC solvent system was preferably selected to investigate the effect of solvent ratio and salt concentration. In the binary PC/EMC (1:1, v/v) system, the highest conductivity of 7.45 mS cm $^{-1}$ at 20 °C is observed at 0.8 M NaPF $_{6}$ (Fig. 1b). It is also found that the conductivity of electrolyte changes with the solvent ratio changing. The viscosity of 0.8 M NaPF $_{6}$ electrolyte is gradually increased with the PC content rising. With an increase in the PC content, the conductivity increases markedly in the range lower than 40%, reaches a maximum at 60% (i.e., PC/EMC=3/2), and inversely declines in the range higher than 60% (Fig. 1c). On the other hand, the electrolytes with PC content lower than 40% are much easier to wet the nonpolar polypropylene-polyethylene separator. Complete wetting of the separator typically takes no more than 10 seconds, as indicated by the wetting angles and wettability in Fig. S1 and Fig. S2. Based on the above results, five 0.8 M NaPF $_{6}$ electrolytes were prepared by using 2 wt% FEC additive and PC/EMC, PC/DMC, EC/EMC, EC/DMC and EC/DEC mixed solvents (all having a 2:3 cyclic/linear carbonate ratio), respectively. It is shown that the ionic conductivity of these electrolytes is increased in the order of EC/DMC > PC/DMC > EC/EMC > PC/EMC > EC/DEC, whereas the viscosity is changed nearly in an opposite order of EC/DEC > EC/EMC > PC/EMC > PC/DMC ≈ EC/DMC (Fig. 2a).

2.1 Electrolyte and pouch cell preparation
Battery grade solvents of propylene carbonate (PC), ethylene carbonate (EC), ethyl methyl carbonate (EMC), dimethyl carbonate (DMC), diethyl carbonate (DEC) and fluoroethylene carbonate (FEC) were obtained from Shenzhen CAPCHEM Technology Co., Ltd, China, and used as received. Sodium hexafluorophosphate $(\mathrm{NaPF}_6$ , KISHIDA Chemical Co., Ltd, Japan) was dissolved into cold solvent mixtures with different volume ratios. Water contents of all resultant electrolytes were determined by the Karl Fischer titration to be lower than $15~\mathrm{ppm}$ .

The $NaNi_{1/3}Fe_{1/3}Mn_{1/3}O_{2}$ (NFM) cathode material was scale-up synthesized as described previously [17]. The NFM cathode and hard carbon (HC) anode were prepared by coating slurries consisting of 92 wt.% active material, 4 wt.% super P, and 4 wt.% polyvinylidene fluoride (PVDF) in N-Methyl-2-pyrrolidone (NMP) onto an aluminum foil, respectively. The cathode-separator-anode assembles were stacked and packaged into a plastic-laminated aluminum pouch. After heating at 80 °C for 48 h under vacuum, the dried pouch cells were moved into a glove box for injecting electrolyte.

The slurry was spread on a copper foil (thickness 18 $\mu$ m) and dried at 80 °C for 8–12 h. Then, it was perforated into a circular electrode sheet with a diameter of 12 mm and a loading of 2.5–3.0 mg cm $^{-2}$ . citations.quote: To verify the practical applicability of CIE, we assembled a 1.2 Ah (163 Wh kg $^{-1}$ ) pouch cell with O3-type NFM positive electrode and HC negative electrode (Fig. 6a). Figure 6b shows the cycling performance of the pouch cell at different temperatures. At 25 °C, the pouch cell provides a capacity of 1.18 Ah. As the temperature decreases, we verify the possibility of its operation at low temperatures, at -50 °C, the pouch cell still provides a capacity of 0.79 Ah (107 Wh kg $^{-1}$ ), demonstrating a significantly better low-temperature adaptability than that of conventional electrolytes. Moreover, even at -50 °C, the charge/discharge curve maintains a stable voltage plateau (Fig. 6c). Figure 6d shows the cycling performance of the pouch cell at -20 °C with 94.1% capacity retention after 300 cycles. In addition, in order to visually verify the practical application potential, the LED lights are continuously powered at a low temperature of -50 °C. The fully-charged state pouch cells keep the LED lights working for more than 10 hours (Fig. 6e). This demonstration confirms that the CIE has good prospects for practical applications, especially at low temperatures. We further compare our results with some previously reported low-temperature sodium-ion pouch cells (Fig. 6f, Table S6) $^{26,52-58}$ , and our work is comparable to most of the advanced reported works, which fully proves that the CIE developed by us has important application value for SIBs in cold environments.

association_citations.quote: To verify the practical applicability of CIE, we assembled a 1.2 Ah (163 Wh kg $^{-1}$ ) pouch cell with O3-type NFM positive electrode and HC negative electrode (Fig. 6a). Figure 6b shows the cycling performance of the pouch cell at different temperatures. At 25 °C, the pouch cell provides a capacity of 1.18 Ah. As the temperature decreases, we verify the possibility of its operation at low temperatures, at -50 °C, the pouch cell still provides a capacity of 0.79 Ah (107 Wh kg $^{-1}$ ), demonstrating a significantly better low-temperature adaptability than that of conventional electrolytes. Moreover, even at -50 °C, the charge/discharge curve maintains a stable voltage plateau (Fig. 6c). Figure 6d shows the cycling performance of the pouch cell at -20 °C with 94.1% capacity retention after 300 cycles. In addition, in order to visually verify the practical application potential, the LED lights are continuously powered at a low temperature of -50 °C. The fully-charged state pouch cells keep the LED lights working for more than 10 hours (Fig. 6e). This demonstration confirms that the CIE has good prospects for practical applications, especially at low temperatures. We further compare our results with some previously reported low-temperature sodium-ion pouch cells (Fig. 6f, Table S6) $^{26,52-58}$ , and our work is comparable to most of the advanced reported works, which fully proves that the CIE developed by us has important application value for SIBs in cold environments.

citations.quote: Firstly, the electrolyte was injected into the pouch NNFM111/HC cells in an argon-filled glove box and then the cells were deposited at room temperature for 24 h. The cells were first charged at 0.1 C constant current for 390 min with a pressure of $3 \, kg cm^{-2}$ . After charging, the cells were put at $45^{\circ}$ C for 24 h with a pressure of $3 \, kg cm^{-2}$ . All cells were activated by charging and discharging at 0.1 C, 0.2 C, 0.5 C, and 1 C. The charge and discharge tests of the NNFM111/HC full cells were conducted using a battery test system (CT-3008 W, Neware, China) at a voltage range of 2.0-4.0 V. The cycle performance of NNFM111/HC full cells was measured at a constant temperature of $25^{\circ}$ C and $45^{\circ}$ C with a charge and discharge current of 1 C. The discharge curves of the NNFM111/HC full cells at $-20^{\circ}$ C were measured in a temperature controlled test chamber at the discharge rates of 0.5 C and 1 C. The ratio of the discharge capacity of the cell at $-20^{\circ}$ C to the last discharge capacity of the cell activated at room temperature was taken as the capacity retention rate of the cell at low temperature. The cells with 50% state of charge (SOC) discharged at a current rate of 2 C for 10 s at $-20^{\circ}$ C. The direct current resistance (DCR) was calculated on the basis of Ohm's law (R=U/I).

A Sodium Bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide (NaFSI)-based Multifunctional Electrolyte Stabilizes the Performance of $NaNi_{1/3}Fe_{1/3}Mn_{1/3}O_{2}/hard\ Carbon\ Sodium-ion\ Batteries$

A sodium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide (NaFSI)-based multifunctional electrolyte is developed by partially replacing $NaPF_{6}$ salt in the electrolyte to improve the wide temperature range working capability of $NaNi_{1/3}Fe_{1/3}Mn_{1/3}O_{2}/hard$ carbon (NNFM111/HC) sodium-ion batteries (SIBs). The capacity retention of the SIBs with NaFSI- $NaPF_{6}$ dual salt electrolyte increases from 47.2% to 75.5% after 250 cycles at 25°C, and from 51.0% to 82.3% after 80 cycles at 45°C, and the 1 C discharge capacity retention at the low temperature of -20°C also increases 26.8%. citations.quote:
Preparation of the Electrolyte
Ethylene carbonate (EC), propylene carbonate (PC), diethyl carbonate (DEC), methyl ethyl carbonate (EMC), dimethyl carbonate (DMC), $NaPF_{6}$ and NaFSI used in the electrolyte are all from the commercial products of Guangzhou Tinci Materials Technology Co., Ltd. and not further purified. The blank electrolyte was a mixture of 1 M $NaPF_{6}$ in EC, PC, EMC and DEC with a ratio of 1:2:6:1 (by weight). NaFSI was added to the blank electrolyte to replace part of $NaPF_{6}$ , maintaining the total content of NaFSI and $NaPF_{6}$ at 1 M. In this work, "blank" represents 1 M $NaPF_{6}$ , "0.1 M NaFSI" represents 0.1 M $NaFSI + 0.9 M NaPF_{6}$ , "0.3 M NaFSI" represents 0.3 M $NaFSI + 0.7 M NaPF_{6}$ , "0.5 M NaFSI" represents 0.5 M $NaFSI + 0.5 M NaPF_{6}$ , "0.7 M NaFSI" represents 0.7 M $NaFSI + 0.3 M NaPF_{6}$ , "0.9 M NaFSI" represents 0.9 M $NaFSI + 0.1 M NaPF_{6}$ . All electrolytes were prepared in an argon-filled glove box with $H_{2}O$ and oxygen concentrations below 0.1 ppm.

However, it is worth noting that the cells using 0.1 M and 0.3 M NaFSI double-salt system decayed rapidly after 100 and 175 cycles, while the cells with 0.5 M NaFSI double-salt system cycled stably. This is because the little content of NaFSI is not enough to form a stable film on the surface of the electrode. As can be seen from Figure 4b, the battery with 0.5 M NaFSI double-salt system still has a capacity retention rate of 75.5% after 250 cycles, while the corresponding value of the single-salt system is only 42.2%. In addition, the coulombic efficiency of the battery with 0.5 M NaFSI double-salt system remained at about 100% during the cycle process, indicating less loss of active sodium.

citations.quote:
4 Conclusions
In summary, we have systematically studied carbonate-based electrolytes for NFM/HC SIBs, showing that PC-based electrolytes outperform in terms of capacity retention and safety, as compared with the EC-based electrolytes. Combined with multiple additives, the PC/EMC electrolyte further promotes the formation of a protective interfacial layer, which consequently mitigates parasitic reactions between the electrodes and electrolyte and suppresses chemical dissolution of transition metal ions from the desodiated (charged) NFM. Finally, we demonstrated that a 0.8 M NaPF $_{6}$ /PC-EMC optimized by the second-generation additives not only enables the NFM/HC pouch cell to reversibly cycle over 2500 cycles but also makes the cell safer.

It is also found that the conductivity of electrolyte changes with the solvent ratio changing. The viscosity of 0.8 M NaPF $_{6}$ electrolyte is gradually increased with the PC content rising. With an increase in the PC content, the conductivity increases markedly in the range lower than 40%, reaches a maximum at 60% (i.e., PC/EMC=3/2), and inversely declines in the range higher than 60% (Fig. 1c). On the other hand, the electrolytes with PC content lower than 40% are much easier to wet the nonpolar polypropylene-polyethylene separator. Complete wetting of the separator typically takes no more than 10 seconds, as indicated by the wetting angles and wettability in Fig. S1 and Fig. S2. Based on the above results, five 0.8 M NaPF $_{6}$ electrolytes were prepared by using 2 wt% FEC additive and PC/EMC, PC/DMC, EC/EMC, EC/DMC and EC/DEC mixed solvents (all having a 2:3 cyclic/linear carbonate ratio), respectively. It is shown that the ionic conductivity of these electrolytes is increased in the order of EC/DMC > PC/DMC > EC/EMC > PC/EMC > EC/DEC, whereas the viscosity is changed nearly in an opposite order of EC/DEC > EC/EMC > PC/EMC > PC/DMC ≈ EC/DMC (Fig. 2a).

2.1 Electrolyte and pouch cell preparation
Battery grade solvents of propylene carbonate (PC), ethylene carbonate (EC), ethyl methyl carbonate (EMC), dimethyl carbonate (DMC), diethyl carbonate (DEC) and fluoroethylene carbonate (FEC) were obtained from Shenzhen CAPCHEM Technology Co., Ltd, China, and used as received. Sodium hexafluorophosphate $(\mathrm{NaPF}_6$ , KISHIDA Chemical Co., Ltd, Japan) was dissolved into cold solvent mixtures with different volume ratios. Water contents of all resultant electrolytes were determined by the Karl Fischer titration to be lower than $15~\mathrm{ppm}$ .

The $NaNi_{1/3}Fe_{1/3}Mn_{1/3}O_{2}$ (NFM) cathode material was scale-up synthesized as described previously [17]. The NFM cathode and hard carbon (HC) anode were prepared by coating slurries consisting of 92 wt.% active material, 4 wt.% super P, and 4 wt.% polyvinylidene fluoride (PVDF) in N-Methyl-2-pyrrolidone (NMP) onto an aluminum foil, respectively. The cathode-separator-anode assembles were stacked and packaged into a plastic-laminated aluminum pouch. After heating at 80 °C for 48 h under vacuum, the dried pouch cells were moved into a glove box for injecting electrolyte.

citations.quote: Electrolyte design strategies are closely related to the capacities, cycle life and safety of sodium-ion batteries. In this study, we are aimed to optimize electrolyte with the focus on engineering aspects. The basic physicochemical properties including ionic conductivity, viscosity, wettability and thermochemical stability of the electrolytes using $\mathrm{NaPF}_6$ as the solute and the mixed solvent with different components of EMC, DMC or DEC in PC or EC were systematically measured. Ah pouch cell with $\mathrm{NaNi}_{1/3}\mathrm{Fe}_{1/3}\mathrm{Mn}_{1/3}\mathrm{O}_2/$ hard carbon electrodes was used to evaluate the performance of the prepared electrolytes. By using the Inductive Coupled Plasma Emission Spectrometer (ICP), X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS), Thermogravimetric-differential scanning calorimetry (TG-DSC) and Accelerating Rate Calorimeter (ARC), we show that an optimized electrolyte can effectively promote the formation of a protective interfacial layer on two electrodes, which not only retards parasitic reactions between the electrodes and electrolyte but also suppresses dissolution of metal ions from the cathode. With an optimized electrolyte, a $NaNi_{1/3}Fe_{1/3}Mn_{1/3}O_{2}$ /hard carbon cell can attain 56.16% capacity retention under the low temperature of -40 °C, and can be able to retain 80% capacity retention after more than 2500 cycles while presenting excellent thermal safety.

citations.quote: To verify the practical applicability of CIE, we assembled a 1.2 Ah (163 Wh kg $^{-1}$ ) pouch cell with O3-type NFM positive electrode and HC negative electrode (Fig. 6a). Figure 6b shows the cycling performance of the pouch cell at different temperatures. At 25 °C, the pouch cell provides a capacity of 1.18 Ah. As the temperature decreases, we verify the possibility of its operation at low temperatures, at -50 °C, the pouch cell still provides a capacity of 0.79 Ah (107 Wh kg $^{-1}$ ), demonstrating a significantly better low-temperature adaptability than that of conventional electrolytes.
